analysis.summary: This is ibuprofen 200 mg, an NSAID pain reliever and fever reducer. It can raise bleeding risk with blood thinners like warfarin, so check with a pharmacist before use. One inactive ingredient may be animal-derived for a vegan diet.

personalFlags.title: Ibuprofen (NSAID) with warfarin
personalFlags.explanation: Ibuprofen is an NSAID. The label says stomach bleeding risk is higher with blood thinners. Confirm with a pharmacist or doctor before using.
personalFlags.evidence: take a blood thinning (anticoagulant) or steroid drug

personalFlags.title: Stearic acid may be animal-derived
personalFlags.explanation: Stearic acid can come from animal or plant sources. The label does not say which. Check with the maker if you follow a vegan diet.

labelWarnings.text: This NSAID may cause severe stomach bleeding. Risk is higher with age 60+, ulcers, alcohol, or taking more than directed.
labelWarnings.evidence: which may cause severe stomach bleeding

labelWarnings.text: NSAIDs can raise the risk of heart attack, heart failure, and stroke. The risk is higher with more or longer use than directed.
labelWarnings.evidence: increase the risk of heart attack, heart failure, and stroke

labelWarnings.text: Ibuprofen may cause a severe allergic reaction, especially in people allergic to aspirin. Stop use and seek medical help if it happens.
labelWarnings.evidence: Ibuprofen may cause a severe allergic reaction

labelWarnings.text: Keep out of reach of children. In case of overdose, get medical help or contact a Poison Control Center right away.
labelWarnings.evidence: Keep out of reach of children.

keyFacts.label: Directions (adults, 12+)
keyFacts.value: Take 1 tablet every 4 to 6 hours while symptoms persist; do not take more than directed

keyFacts.label: Inactive ingredients
keyFacts.value: carnauba wax, colloidal silicon dioxide, corn starch, hypromellose, iron oxide, polyethylene glycol, stearic acid, titanium dioxide

analysis.disclaimer: This explains the label and is not medical advice. Ask a pharmacist or doctor about taking this with warfarin; in case of overdose, call local emergency services or poison control right away.
